text:
micah: Heads-up — we need to decide how to surface auth telemetry for API keys vs org/project in the console. Current ingestion stores key_id and project_id on every request. Privacy/legal are asking for sampling options. thoughts?

sara: +1 on sampling. We shouldn't keep raw key IDs in the observability store by default. Keep full records only for billing/audit pipeline.

raj: Concern: billing attribution relies on exact counts. If we sample indiscriminately we risk billing mismatches. Idea: split the pipelines — full fidelity -> billing, sampled/hashed -> observability.

jia: UX tradeoff: if metrics are sampled we'll need to annotate charts. Users will be confused if console numbers differ from billing. propose: show sampled metrics with a small badge and an explicit link to billing numbers.

micah: Agreed. Operational plan sketch: route every request to a lightweight router that marks it for either "billing" or "observability". Billing gets unmodified key/project (encrypted at rest, strict retention). Observability gets hashed key_id and is sampled (default 5%).

sara: From compliance: hashed IDs may still be considered identifying in some jurisdictions. We need org-level opt-out and per-region settings. Also retention SLAs: observability hashed data 30d raw, 90d aggregates. Billing raw logs 365d encrypted.

raj: Implementation note: prefer a small LUT at the edge to avoid an extra DB lookup per request. The LUT consults: org-feature-flag (auth:telemetry_split) and header X-Billing-Attribution. If header present -> billing.

micah: Example routing config proposed: 
```
routing:
  - if: header.X-Billing-Attribution == "true"
    pipeline: billing
  - else:
    pipeline: observability
sampling:
  observability: 0.05
```

jia: On the console side: charts that use observability pipeline should show a tiny "sampled" badge with hover showing sample rate and time window. For audit logs show the complete un-sampled list but gated by org permissions.

sara: Legal checklist: add KMS encryption for billing logs, add retention policy enforcement, update DPA/FAQ for customers, and an opt-out toggle in the tenant settings. I'll draft language.

raj: For rollout: canary on a low-traffic region with flag enabled for selected orgs. Deploy steps: push routing LUT + sampling config -> enable feature flag for 10 orgs -> monitor discrepancy between billed tokens and sampled extrapolation.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan queued: /deploy auth-telemetry-split --canary=10% --regions=us-west1 --tag=telemetry-split

micah: Metrics to watch during canary: billing_count_vs_sampled_extrapolation, per-org mismatch, ingest-latency, edge-router-error-rate. Add an automatic alert if mismatch > 2% for 30m.

jia: UX follow-ups: mockup for badge + tooltip, and a small explainer in the key detail flyout that tells users why numbers differ. I'll post mocks by EOD Friday.

raj: I'll open a PR with the router code and config schema (sample_rate, retention, routing rules). Will include unit tests for header-based routing and feature-flag gating.

sara: Also remind infra to add a KMS rotation runbook for billing logs and to ensure access control for the audit view.

micah: Action items: raj -> prototype LUT + PR; jia -> console badge mocks; sara -> legal + retention text; I'll schedule the canary next Tue and own the monitoring dashboards.

sara: +1. Also add a note to the onboarding docs so customers understand the telemetry split (FAQ + opt-out).

raj: Posting link to initial schema draft in the PR once it's up.

micah: Thanks all — tagging @jia and @raj for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
